narrative.overview:
The page is a control tower seen from the side: a second monitor that stays lit while the user works on the main one. Like flight strips on a controller's desk, each session is one quiet line that changes in place, and only one clearance is handed over at a time. The tower never shouts; it holds. Whatever arrives while the user is reading waits its turn in plain sight.

The look is a dark, flat instrument panel. Surfaces separate by tone and a single hairline, not by shadow. One warm amber carries attention, red marks what holds on the user, green clears, blue reports. Type is the system stack at a compact operational density: the decision summary is the only large text, every section heading is a small uppercase caption. Light mode exists and follows the OS (`prefers-color-scheme`); dark is the reference.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, flat, tonal layering; no shadows.
One warm accent (amber) and three signal colors (red, green, blue), each with a fixed meaning.
System font stack, 15px body, 11px uppercase captions, one 19px headline per screen.
Two columns: the decision on the left, the plan cycle in a sticky 380px column on the right.
Keyboard affordances printed on screen (`1`, `2`… key caps, hint line under the card).

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: In the session strip, colour means "waits on you": an amber square is your decision, a red square an approval blocking a session; living sessions stay neutral round lamps (grey working, hollow idle, green done). Elsewhere red only marks Deny and breakage, green clears, blue informs. Shape and the state word always double the colour. Tints are derived with `color-mix()` against `--panel` at 12–14% for banner grounds and 30–45% for their borders, never new hex values.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Every color comes from the ten `:root` custom properties, redefined once for light mode. The only literal is `#111` text on the amber button.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Only the card summary is large. Everything else is body, dense body or caption, so the eye lands on the decision first from across the desk.

rules.name: The Still Column Rule
rules.body: Nothing re-renders under the pointer or the focus. The right column skips updates while hovered or focused, and the displayed card is never replaced until it is answered; later cards wait as pills in "Ensuite".

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows. Emphasis comes from border color (amber, red, green) and the Amber Wash ground, never from lifting a surface.

dos: Do take every color from the ten `:root` tokens and their light-mode redefinition; derive tints with `color-mix()`.
Do keep colour for what waits on you: amber square = your decision, red square = blocked on your approval; everything else in the strip stays neutral.
Do print the keyboard shortcut next to the control it triggers (key caps, "(N)", "↵", the hint line).
Do use `tabular-nums` for any time, count or ratio that updates in place.
Do keep section captions at 11px uppercase grey so the card summary stays the only loud text.
donts: Don't add drop shadows or elevation; separate by tone and 1px borders.
Don't animate, auto-scroll or reflow content the user may be reading; the card and the hovered column hold still.
Don't add "new" badges or highlight outlines to announce changes; the away banner is the only catch-up.
